previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old man with a history of coronary artery disease, prior stents, diabetes, and diastolic heart failure was admitted for pleuritic chest pain lasting three days. The pain was positional and worse with inspiration, differing from prior myocardial infarctions. Initial evaluation showed normal troponins, no EKG evidence of acute ischemia, and a normal echocardiogram. A nuclear stress test was normal, and imaging ruled out pulmonary embolism and aortic dissection. The clinical picture was consistent with pericarditis. The patient responded well to acetaminophen and symptom management, with no complications. Chronic conditions including diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and heart failure were managed with continued medications. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions for pain control, weight monitoring, and cardiology follow-up.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  Chest pain.

TECHNIQUE:  Supine AP view of the chest.

COMPARISON:  ___.

FINDINGS:

Heart size is normal.  Mediastinal and hilar contours are unchanged, with mild
calcification of the aortic knob is noted.  The lungs are clear and the
pulmonary vasculature is normal.  No focal consolidation, pleural effusion or
pneumothorax is visualized.  There are no acute osseous abnormalities.

IMPRESSION:

No acute cardiopulmonary abnormality.

INDICATION:  Chest pain, elevated D-dimer, evaluate for pulmonary embolism.

COMPARISON:  CTA chest from ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Contiguous axial MDCT images were obtained through the chest
during and after the administration of 100 cc Omnipaque intravenous contrast. 
Axial images were reviewed in conjunction with coronal and sagittal reformats.

FINDINGS:

CTA CHEST:  Pulmonary arteries are well opacified to the subsegmental level. 
Nonocclusive thrombus is seen in the left upper and lower lobar, segmental and
subsegmental pulmonary artery branches.  There is also nonocclusive thrombus
seen in the right lower lobe pulmonary artery, extending into the segmental
level, and within several of the distal subsegmental branches. No evidence of
right heart strain is seen. Numerous coronary arterial stents are
demonstrated. Thoracic aorta is of normal caliber without evidence of aneurysm
or dissection.

CT CHEST:  Thyroid is homogeneous.  There is no mediastinal or hilar
lymphadenopathy by CT size criteria.  Trachea is midline and airways are
patent to the subsegmental level.  The inferior aspect of lung bases is not
completely imaged.  Mild bronchiectasis within the lung bases is again noted. 
There are no focal areas of consolidation.  There is no pleural effusion and
no pneumothorax.

Limited view of the upper abdomen is unremarkable.  Bones are intact without
suspicious lesions.

IMPRESSION:
Bilateral pulmonary emboli within the left upper and lower lobar, segmental
and subsegmental branches as well as the right lower lobar, segmental, and
subsegmental branches.  There is no evidence of right heart strain.

HISTORY:  ___ man with bilateral PEs, evaluate legs for DVT.

COMPARISON:  Bilateral leg ultrasound ___.

FINDINGS:

Grayscale, color and Doppler images were obtained of bilateral common femoral,
femoral, popliteal and tibial veins.

There is acute deep vein thrombosis seen within the left common femoral vein
extending into the proximal and mid portions of the left femoral vein.  A
small portion of the thrombus is also seen extending into the greater
saphenous vein, just at the sapheno femoral junction.  The greater saphenous
vein demonstrates normal compression in the mid thigh.

Normal compression, flow and augmentation is seen in the distal portion of the
left femoral vein and in the left popliteal and tibial veins.  The veins of
the right leg demonstrate normal flow, compression and augmentation.

IMPRESSION:

Acute deep vein thrombosis seen in the left common femoral and femoral veins
and also minimally extending into the left greater saphenous vein.
